chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Isma'il ibn Sa'd al-Ash'ari said:
I asked al-Rida (peace be upon him) about the woman whose menstruation is irregular (mustarabah), how is she divorced? He said, 'She is divorced by months.'

key_terms.الرِّضَا: Al-Rida (peace be upon him), referring to Imam Ali al-Rida
key_terms.الْمُسْتَرَابَةِ: The woman with irregular menstruation whose cycle is uncertain
key_terms.بِالشُّهُورِ: By months, indicating the method of calculating the waiting period

ai.seo_question: How is the divorce of a woman with irregular menstruation determined in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) establishes that for a woman with irregular menstruation (mustarabah), the divorce timing is determined by counting three lunar months, a ruling derived from the Quranic verse on 'those who have no hope of menstruation.' This specific application highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on adapting the general Quranic principle of 'three months' to the unique physiological condition of mustarabah, distinguishing it from the standard three menstrual cycles prescribed for regular cases.
